title.narrative: B-NEX: Better Nutrition through Emergency Cross-sectoral interventions (Agriculture, WASH, and Health)

description.narrative: ltpgtGida Ayana is one of the most neglected areas regarding malnutrition, primarily due to movement restrictions and ongoing insecurity in the East Wollega Zone of the Oromia region (RGE, 2024). The woreda has a total population of 158,000 and hosts one of the largest numbers of returnees and internally displaced persons (IDPs). Recent assessments indicate that there are approximately 14,598 returnees and 21,725 IDPs in the woreda, of which 11,378 are female (Positive Action for Development [PAD], 2025).ltbrgtThe ongoing conflict has severely impacted livelihoods, with many returnees losing their farmland, livestock, and other sources of income, contributing to alarming levels of malnutrition. A recent screening of children under five revealed a Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rate of 34%, with a Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) rate estimated at 17%, both of which exceed the emergency threshold (PAD, 2025 Woreda Health Office, 2025). Although therapeutic feeding programs are partially operational, they frequently face stockouts of essential supplies, such as F-75 and F-100. The assessment report also highlighted that Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) services are non-functional, exacerbated by a critical shortage of trained staff and outreach capacity. Additionally, road blockages caused by ongoing conflict continue to restrict movement and access to essential services within the woreda.ltbrgtCommunities face significant challenges in accessing clean water, sanitation services, and health care. Currently, 70% of health facilities are partially damaged, while 22% are completely non-functional (Woreda Health Office, 2025). Furthermore, 15 Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) facilities are not operational in the target woreda (PAD, 2025).ltbrgtIn response to these challenges, PAD and the Action for Social Development and Environmental Protection Organization (ASDEPO) have designed a project aimed at improving the nutritional status of affected communities through cross-sectoral interventions in Nutrition, Agriculture, WASH, and Health. The proposed interventions align with the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and directly contribute to cluster objectives. The project will support Strategic Objective One (SO1) by addressing the needs of people affected by conflict and violence, and Strategic Objective Two (SO2) by ensuring agile support for basic service provision in hard-to-reach areas. Additionally, it will contribute to Strategic Objective Three (SO3) by providing critical assistance to communities displaced in 2024 and earlier, who are still recovering from the ongoing conflict in the target area. This initiative is closely aligned with the priority areas outlined in the Emergency Health Fund (EHF) 2025 First Standard Allocation Paper and reflects the priorities of both the Regional Government and the targeted woreda.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented from August 1, 2025, to July 31, 2026, in Gida Ayana Woreda of East Wollega Zone, with a total budget of $1,000,000. The implementation will be carried out by PAD and ASDEPO in collaboration with local stakeholders. A total of 62,781 individuals will be targeted in this project, of whom 58% (36,392 individuals) are female. Among the total beneficiaries, 4,278 individuals will be people with disabilities, with females accounting for 2,828. The consortium will work closely with relevant stakeholders at various levels to achieve the project objectives.ltbrgtlt/pgt
